Downloading AgERA5 data with ag5Tools

ag5Tools.Rmd

Overview

The Copernicus “Agrometeorological indicators from 1979 to present derived from reanalysis” dataset (AgERA5) provides daily surface meteorological data at 0.1° (~11 km) resolution from 1979 to present. The ag5_download() function gives programmatic access to this dataset from R via the Copernicus Climate Data Store (CDS) API.

Each downloaded file covers one day and one variable, stored as a NetCDF (.nc) file. Across a full year that means 365 (or 366) files per variable, one per day.

Setup

1. Register with the CDS

Create a free account at https://cds.climate.copernicus.eu.

2. Get your API key

After logging in, your API key is shown on your profile page. Follow the instructions at the CDS API Guide to create a .cdsapirc configuration file in your home directory containing your key.

3. Python and cdsapi

ag5Tools calls the CDS via the Python cdsapi library using the reticulate package. If Python or cdsapi are not installed, ag5_download() will install them automatically on first use.

Available variables

ag5_download() uses the CDS API variable names (snake_case). These differ from the file names written to disk, which are used by ag5_extract(). See vignette("extracing_data") for the mapping between the two naming systems.

Variable (CDS API name) Description
2m_temperature 2 m air temperature (multiple statistics)
2m_dewpoint_temperature 2 m dew point temperature
2m_relative_humidity 2 m relative humidity (specific times of day)
precipitation_flux Daily precipitation (mm/day)
liquid_precipitation_duration_fraction Fraction of day with liquid precipitation
solid_precipitation_duration_fraction Fraction of day with solid precipitation
solar_radiation_flux Daily solar radiation (J/m²/day)
vapour_pressure Daily mean vapour pressure
10m_wind_speed 10 m wind speed
cloud_cover Daily mean cloud cover
snow_thickness Snow depth
snow_thickness_lwe Snow liquid water equivalent

Statistics

Some variables are available with multiple daily statistics. Provide the statistic name in the statistic argument.

2m_temperature — must specify one of:

Statistic Description
24_hour_maximum Maximum over 24 hours
24_hour_mean Mean over 24 hours
24_hour_minimum Minimum over 24 hours
day_time_maximum Maximum during daytime
day_time_mean Mean during daytime
night_time_mean Mean during night-time
night_time_minimum Minimum during night-time

10m_wind_speed, vapour_pressure, cloud_cover, 2m_dewpoint_temperature — only 24_hour_mean is available. The statistic argument must be provided.

precipitation_flux, solar_radiation_flux, snow_thickness, snow_thickness_lwe, liquid_precipitation_duration_fraction, solid_precipitation_duration_fraction — no statistic argument needed.

2m_relative_humidity — no statistic, but requires a time argument: "06_00", "09_00", "12_00", "15_00", or "18_00".

Downloading data

A single day 

library(ag5Tools)

ag5_download(
  variable  = "2m_temperature",
  statistic = "24_hour_maximum",
  year      = 2015,
  month     = 6,
  day       = 15,
  path      = "C:/agera5_data"
)

All days in a month

Set day = "all" to download every day of the specified month.

ag5_download(
  variable  = "precipitation_flux",
  year      = 2015,
  month     = 6,
  day       = "all",
  path      = "C:/agera5_data"
)

An entire year

Set both month = "all" and day = "all" to download a full year.

ag5_download(
  variable  = "solar_radiation_flux",
  year      = 2020,
  month     = "all",
  day       = "all",
  path      = "C:/agera5_data"
)

Relative humidity (requires time) 

ag5_download(
  variable = "2m_relative_humidity",
  time     = "09_00",
  year     = 2015,
  month    = "all",
  day      = "all",
  path     = "C:/agera5_data"
)

Spatial subsetting with area

By default ag5_download() downloads the full global extent. Use the area argument to restrict the download to a region of interest — this substantially reduces file size and download time.

Bounding box

Provide a numeric vector c(north, west, south, east) in decimal degrees.

# East Africa bounding box
ag5_download(
  variable  = "2m_temperature",
  statistic = "24_hour_maximum",
  year      = 2015,
  month     = "all",
  day       = "all",
  area      = c(5, 28, -12, 42),
  path      = "C:/agera5_data"
)

Single point

Provide c(lon, lat). A minimum 0.1° bounding box (one AgERA5 grid cell) is derived automatically.

ag5_download(
  variable  = "2m_temperature",
  statistic = "24_hour_maximum",
  year      = 2015,
  month     = "all",
  day       = "all",
  area      = c(36.68, -3.37),   # lon, lat — Arusha, Tanzania
  path      = "C:/agera5_data"
)

File organisation on disk

Downloaded files follow the naming convention used by the CDS and are organised into sub-folders by variable and statistic automatically. For example, daily maximum temperature files for 2015 will appear under a path such as:

C:/agera5_data/
  Temperature-Air-2m/
    Max-24h/
      AgERA5_Temperature-Air-2m_Max-24h_20150101.nc
      AgERA5_Temperature-Air-2m_Max-24h_20150102.nc
      ...

ag5_extract() searches the folder tree recursively, so you only need to provide the root path when extracting.
